Priya K.: Customer reported search re-rank job failing after we rolled a pinned model change this morning. They send: `Indexing error: embedding vector length mismatch: expected 1536, got 1024`

Priya K.: Customer originally pinned `redwood-embed-v1.2` two weeks ago, then we did a safety mapping that moved some traffic to `redwood-embed-v1.2-compat` during the upgrade window. After the canary, they started seeing mismatches.

Mateo R.: Can you paste the exact API call they used? need to repro locally.

Priya K.: They used our embeddings endpoint via curl, sample provided by customer:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer <KEY>\" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-v1.2","input":["hello world"]}'
```

Priya K.: Response failure from their client: `400 Bad Request` payload: `{\"error\":\"vector length mismatch: expected 1536, got 1024\"}`

Jake S.: That screams model variant mismatch — either the model we return changed dimensionality or the catalog entry mapping for that pinned alias pointed to a different architecture. I'll try calling the same model id from the catalog.

Alexis L.: @Jake S. note that some of the -compat artifacts are quantized and return smaller vector sizes in older infra. Might be our migration script left some alias entries pointing to a quantized variant.

Jake S.: Reproduced locally hitting the pinned alias: when I call `redwood-embed-v1.2` via the control-plane mapping I get back vector length 1024. When I call the canonical artifact `redwood-embed-v1.2-archA` I get 1536. So alias -> artifact mapping is inconsistent.

Mateo R.: Logged the mapping table entry: `alias redwood-embed-v1.2 -> artifact redwood-embed-v1.2-quant` (unexpected). Looks like the upgrade job replaced the alias to point at a smaller-dim quantized variant to save memory during canary.

Priya K.: Customer expectation: pinned alias should always return same vector size. They were depending on 1536 dims for downstream index.

Support Bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1837 - embeddings-vector-dim-mismatch-on-pinned-alias

Jake S.: Immediate mitigation options: 1) Re-point alias back to `redwood-embed-v1.2-archA` (fast) 2) Provide a temporary server-side pad/trim transform for their calls (adds latency/cost) 3) Ask them to reindex with new dim (high customer effort).

Priya K.: Customer wants minimal work on their side. Please do option 1 if safe.

Mateo R.: I will coordinate a hotfix: revert alias mapping for pinned customer accounts to prior artifact. Doing this per-customer avoids breaking other tenants who intentionally moved to the quant variant.

Alexis L.: Note: we must also detect any other aliases that were moved to quantized artifacts during the automated reroute. I'll run a quick diff against the backup mapping snapshot from before the deploy.

Jake S.: Patch prepared: PR #4861 will add a safety-check preventing alias rebinds in the 1-hour post-upgrade window for pinned models, and an alert when alias dimension changes. Deploying to control-plane now.

Priya K.: Pushed the customer fix at 15:24 UTC: alias reverted. Customer ran the same curl and now receives 1536-dim vectors. They confirmed indexing resumed. :tada:

Mateo R.: Root cause: our upgrade workflow temporarily maps aliases to memory-optimized quantized artifacts for canary traffic. A subset of aliases that had explicit pins in the DB were not excluded due to a filter bug (missing `pinned=true` guard). This allowed a pinned alias to be bound to the quant artifact.

Alexis L.: Follow-ups: 1) add integration test that asserts alias->artifact dim stays constant for pinned models 2) backfill a migration tool to detect customers who have pinned aliases pointing at artifacts with unexpected dims and notify them 3) add a telemetry metric for alias-dim delta.

Jake S.: For the customer we also offered a temporary API-level shim: if the client cannot reindex immediately, we can provide a per-customer padding layer that will zero-pad 1024->1536 (or trim if the reverse happens). This is best-effort and will carry a perf hit; customer declined — they were happy with alias revert.

Priya K.: Customer requested a postmortem and a written note they can share internally. I've scheduled a handoff to CSM and will include root cause summary, the mitigation we performed, and the suggested long-term options (reindex, pinned-model checks, shim).

Support Bot: Patch release note queued: \"Fix: prevent alias rebind to quant/variant artifacts for pinned models; add alert on alias vector-dim changes\"

eng-oncall-bot: Deploy succeeded: control-plane v2.14.1 -> rolled out to 3 control-plane regions.

Mateo R.: Action items (short):
- [ ] Backfill mapping snapshot diff and alert any other affected customers (Mateo)
- [ ] Add integration test & unit for pinned alias guard (Jake)
- [ ] Postmortem doc and customer-facing note (Priya)

Priya K.: Customer follow-up: they want confirmation when the integration test lands. I'll keep them in the loop.

Alexis L.: Also creating a small diagnostic tool we can give customers: a single curl that validates their expected dimension against the pinned alias. Something like:```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" -d '{"model":"<alias>","input":["test"]}' | jq '.data[0].embedding | length'
```

Priya K.: Thanks all — closing thread for now after the customer ack. I'll attach the PM notes to INC-2026-1837 and tag in the postmortem when ready.

Jake S.: Leaving a note: if we ever need to pad/trim in-shape, prefer deterministic zero-padding and add a metric to count padded responses.

Support Bot: Thread closed by Priya K.
